newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Sept 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.

China's Premier Li Peng said in the opening ceremony of the 21st Century Forum, attended by statesmen from around the world, that China opposed hegemony and power politics, and offered a proposal for Asia's development based on equality and cooperation.
A commentary says that too many of the nation's historical and cultural sites were being exploited and commercialised.
Shenzhen stock exchange overtook Shanghai in overall trading volume in the January-August period.
China announced incentives to speed up technical renovations in enterprises.
China would place most foreign government loans and aid projects in the country's less developed western and central regions.
Poeple's Construction Bank of China granted another 2.6 billion yuan loans to key industries.
Editorial attacked florid advertisements of listed companies and misleading reports of corporate results.
Chaotic accounting management caused nearly 100 billion yuan losses in public funds each year.
China's Eximbank signed a $10 million export credit agreement with Kenya bank.
Financial experts said China's lending rates were too low and called for the removal of ceiling on rates to curb corruption and other irregularities.
State Information Centre said 60 to 80 percent of the mobile phones on the market were smuggled into the country.
